title: Powers and Roots: Squares, Cubes, Square Roots and Cube Roots
seo_title: Year 7 Powers and Roots Worksheets: Squares, Cubes, Square Roots, Cube Roots and Index Notation
standard_text: Use integer powers and associated real roots (square, cube and higher), recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, 5 and distinguish between exact representations of roots and their decimal approximations.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 powers and roots worksheets: squares and cubes, square roots and cube roots, index notation, estimating square roots and problems with area and volume. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: 5² = 5 × 5 = 25, and √25 = 5. A square root undoes a square.
key_sub: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, and ∛8 = 2. To estimate √50, use the squares either side: 49 and 64.
body_html:
How it works

A power tells you how many times to multiply a number by itself: 5² = 5 × 5 = 25 and 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

A square root undoes squaring: √25 = 5. A cube root undoes cubing: ∛8 = 2.

To estimate √50, find the square numbers either side: 49 = 7² and 64 = 8², so √50 is just over 7.

Example

Work out 3⁴.

3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81.

Answer: 81

Example

Work out √144 + 2³.

√144 = 12 and 2³ = 8.

12 + 8 = 20.

Answer: 20

Example

Work out (−6)².

(−6) × (−6) = 36: two negatives make a positive.

Answer: 36

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying by the power: 5² is 25, not 10.
  • Halving for a square root: √36 is 6, not 18.
  • Adding under the root: √9 + √16 = 3 + 4 = 7, but √25 = 5.
  • Mixing up 2⁵ and 5²: 2⁵ = 32 and 5² = 25.

faq.q: What is the difference between 5² and 5 × 2?
faq.a: 5² means 5 × 5 = 25. 5 × 2 = 10. The small 2 says how many fives to multiply.

How do I estimate a square root?
faq.a: Find the two square numbers either side. √50 is between √49 = 7 and √64 = 8, and closer to 7.

faq.q: Can a square number be negative?
faq.a: No. A positive or negative number squared is always positive or zero, for example (−4)² = 16.
